s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of disorganized speech, anxiety, and self-harm behaviors with rapid progression of cognitive and psychiatric symptoms
salient_findings: Disorganized speech with rapid and fluent but nonsensical phrases
Severe anxiety and self-harm behaviors
Development of agitation, persecutory delusions, and hallucinations
Urinary and fecal incontinence
Significant cognitive impairment with disorientation and poor performance on cognitive tests
key_facts: 74-year-old right-handed woman
5-month history of symptoms
Abrupt onset of symptoms after a family trip
History of depression treated with sertraline
No prior cognitive impairment or neurological disease
Disoriented to time
Demonstrated anomia and perseveration
Impaired performance on cognitive tests
Normal brain MRI 2 months after symptom onset
Started on memantine and quetiapine without clinical improvement

shortlist.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of cognitive and psychiatric symptoms, normal brain MRI, and lack of response to Alzheimer's disease treatment

shortlist.label: Frontotemporal dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of disorganized speech, anxiety, and self-harm behaviors with prominent frontal and temporal features

shortlist.label: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abrupt onset of symptoms, psychiatric features, and cognitive decline, with potential for rapid progression

shortlist.label: Hashimoto's encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of cognitive and psychiatric symptoms, with potential for autoimmune etiology

shortlist.label: Prion disease
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of cognitive and psychiatric symptoms, with potential for prion disease given the acute onset and lack of response to treatment

raw.rationale: The patient's abrupt onset of symptoms, rapid progression, and combination of cognitive, psychiatric, and neurological features are consistent with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, a rare prion disease characterized by rapid decline and multifocal neurological deficits.

rejected.label: Frontotemporal dementia
rejected.why: Typically has a more gradual onset and slower progression

rejected.label: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis
rejected.why: Usually presents with prominent psychiatric symptoms and seizures, and often has a teratoma or other tumor

rejected.label: Hashimoto's encephalopathy
rejected.why: Typically has a more gradual onset and is associated with thyroid autoantibodies

rejected.label: Prion disease
rejected.why: Too broad, as Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease is a specific type of prion disease
